How we work

  • Write. The writer opens an account with their own money, plays, requests a withdrawal and records what happens.
  • Verify. A second team member re-checks the licence number, bonus terms and payout timings against the operator's own pages and the regulator's register.
  • Date. Each review carries a visible last-updated date and the names of both people involved.
  • Revisit. Bonuses, banking limits and licences change, so pages are re-tested and re-dated rather than quietly edited.

The full method, including how each scoring category is weighted, is set out in our editorial guidelines. Profiles for every team member are on the writers page, and the reasoning behind our ratings is explained in why trust us.

Why two names appear on every review

A single reviewer can be wrong in good faith. They can misread a rollover clause, trust a licence badge without looking the number up, or get one unusually fast withdrawal and generalise from it. The second name on each page exists to catch exactly that: an independent repeat of the licence lookup, the bonus arithmetic and at least one full deposit-and-withdrawal cycle. Where the two disagree, nothing publishes until the discrepancy is settled.

This is also why several brands we cover score poorly. Verification found claims that could not be substantiated — an unverifiable Malta licence on one site, an unconfirmed Curaçao claim on another, a regulator named only in general terms on a third. Those findings stayed in the reviews rather than being smoothed over.

Independence

No operator sees a review before it publishes, and none can pay for placement, a score or a ranking position. We do not sell backlinks or guest posts. Writers do not review brands they have any commercial relationship with, and nobody verifies their own work. The site is funded by affiliate commission, explained in full on our about page.

Corrections

Spotted something out of date? Tell us. We verify every report ourselves and publish confirmed corrections with a new date stamp rather than editing quietly, so the change stays visible.
